match.reason: The bank card 'Negative indices' covers rewriting negative indices as reciprocals, but the new point also requires applying the index laws to expressions with negative indices and giving positive-index answers, which the card does not teach.

draft.title: Negative indices with pronumerals
card: A negative index means a reciprocal. \(x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^{n}}\). The index moves the power to the other side of the fraction line, and the sign of the index changes.
A number in front is not affected. In \(3x^{-2}\), only \(x\) has the index \(-2\). So \(3x^{-2} = \frac{3}{x^{2}}\), not \(\frac{1}{3x^{2}}\).
The index laws still work with negative indices. Multiplying adds the indices, and dividing subtracts them. \(x^{5} \times x^{-8} = x^{-3}\).
Finish with positive indices. Example: \(\frac{6x^{2}}{2x^{5}} = 3x^{2-5} = 3x^{-3}\), which is \(\frac{3}{x^{3}}\).
draft.remember: A negative index means the power belongs on the other side of the fraction line, and only the pronumeral moves.

a.q: Which expression is \(5y^{-3}\) written with a positive index?
a.why: Only \(y\) has the index \(-3\), so only \(y^{3}\) moves to the denominator and the 5 stays on top. \(\frac{1}{5y^{3}}\) is tempting, but it wrongly moves the 5 as well.
a.clue: Which part of the term has the negative index?

b.q: Simplify \(\frac{12a^{3}}{4a^{7}}\), giving the answer with a positive index.
b.why: Divide the numbers: \(12 \div 4 = 3\). Subtract the indices: \(3 - 7 = -4\), so we get \(3a^{-4} = \frac{3}{a^{4}}\). \(3a^{4}\) comes from subtracting the indices the wrong way round.
b.clue: Subtract the index on the bottom from the index on top, then fix the sign.

problems.detail: 'Only the pronumeral moves' overgeneralises the card. The card says only the base that carries the negative index moves (in 3x^{-2}, the 3 stays). A student could wrongly apply the line to (5y)^{-3} or 2^{-3}, where the number does move, or to terms like x^{-2}y^{3}, where not every pronumeral moves.

check.summary: Both questions and their answers are correct. The remember line 'only the pronumeral moves' overgeneralises: it is the base with the negative index that moves, which can be a number or a bracket.
